title: Challenge: manage images (pull, tag, inspect, clean up)
intro: An image is the blueprint a container is started from. Pull one, see what you have, give it a friendlier name, peek at its layers, and remove it. (Commands are checked, not executed, so practice freely.)

steps.instruction: Pull the small 'alpine:3.20' image from Docker Hub.
steps.success:
3.20: Pulling from library/alpine
2d1f4bdf: Pull complete
Digest: sha256:1d34ff...
Status: Downloaded newer image for alpine:3.20

REPOSITORY   TAG    IMAGE ID       SIZE
alpine       3.20   1d34ff8a1b2c   7.8MB

steps.instruction: Give it a friendlier name: tag alpine:3.20 as 'myapp:1.0'.
steps.success: (no output) myapp:1.0 now points at the SAME image id as alpine:3.20

steps.instruction: Inspect how the image was built, layer by layer.
steps.success:
IMAGE          CREATED       CREATED BY                          SIZE
1d34ff8a1b2c   2 weeks ago   /bin/sh -c #(nop) CMD ["/bin/sh"]    0B
<missing>      2 weeks ago   /bin/sh -c #(nop) ADD file:... in /  7.8MB
steps.fail: Use docker history <image> to see its layers.

steps.instruction: Remove the 'myapp:1.0' tag to clean up.
steps.success:
Untagged: myapp:1.0
(the underlying alpine:3.20 image stays, it is still referenced)
steps.fail: Remove the image tag with docker rmi <image>.

done: Solved! pull -> images -> tag -> history -> rmi. A tag is just a label pointing at an image id; removing a tag only deletes the image data when nothing else references it.
